transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-05 16:00 PST - Duration 62 mins
Attendees: Liam C (Redwood AE), Aisha P (Redwood SE), Maya S (Redwood Partnerships); Carlos M, Priya K, Tom B, Sara L (Zenith)

[00:00] Liam Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. i'm liam from redwood, i'll kick us off. can folks state where they're dialing in from?
[00:12] Carlos Mendes: carlos, zenith infra, san paulo office, uh - excited to talk through partnership.
[00:17] Priya Kapoor: priya here, cloud partnerships, bay area.
[00:20] Tom Brewer: tom, product - GPUs and infra.
[00:23] Sara Li: sara, solutions architect, seattle.
[00:26] Aisha Patel: aisha from redwood, solutions eng, i'll cover the tech bits.

[00:34] Liam Chen: quick agenda: intros, phone through partner models (resell, managed infra, co-sell), integration constraints (v p c, on prem, kms), then technical questions and next steps.

[01:02] Tom Brewer: to be clear, zenith is a hardware/cloud vendor - we sell racks with A100-ish and upcoming X-1 chips; we also run a managed region in eu and na. curious how redwood thinks about dedicated pools vs private vpc installs.
[01:20] Aisha Patel: yeah great q. redwood offers three modes: hosted api, dedicated (reserved GPU pools in our infra), and private deploy where the control plane can be customer managed. for partners the main patterns are: 1) we run redwood dedicated on partner-hosted hardware (we'd provision instances on your clusters), or 2) we ship a private bundle that you or the customer run behind their v p c. both need network peering and k e y mgmt integration.
[01:48] Sara Li: when you say control plane, is it a managed control plane or do you hand over everything for air-gapped installs?
[01:55] Aisha Patel: we have a hybrid. for fully air-gapped we provide an on-prem package, but that requires some installation windows and an ops handover. the managed private control plane can sit in your tenant with SSO/SAML and customer KMS hooks.

[02:20] Priya Kapoor: security is big for our enterprise customers. they ask for SOC2, audit logs, and HSM integrations. do you have SOC2 and KMS support?
[02:28] Liam Chen: yes, we are SOC2 and have KMS integrations for hosted and private. for dedicated on partner infra we'd need to align on key access patterns - you can bring your own KMS or we can use vaulted keys in your HSM.

[03:05] Carlos Mendes: one thing - latency SLAs. some customers want single-digit ms for short prompts, others ok with throughput. how does redwood control routing and fallback?
[03:16] Aisha Patel: we do smart routing policy, you can route by latency tier or cost. in partner deployments we usually implement local inference pools for low-latency routes and fall back to other regions or lower-cost models if capacity is constrained. also prefix / KV caching helps for repeat queries.

[03:45] Tom Brewer: curious about the kernel selection piece - do you ship custom runtimes for different chips? our X-1 has different tensor core layouts.
[03:55] Aisha Patel: yes, we have a compilation layer that picks kernels per architecture and sequence length distribution. for new chips we run a small onboarding: profiler runs, microbenchmarks, and then a tuned kernel set. that's part of the model onboarding work.

[04:12] Speaker 1: (inaudible) -- sorry could you repeat the onboarding steps?
[04:18] Aisha Patel: sure. step one is bench: we run sample models (LLM small/medium) with representative sequences. step two is config - batching, KV cache, quantization profiles. step three is rollout - canary + A/B. the profiler gives kernel choices.

[05:05] Priya Kapoor: for a partner story, are you looking for resell, managed service, or ISV OEM?
[05:12] Liam Chen: we're open to multiple. typical partner pilot: we co-sell where zenith provides infra and sales intro, we provide the runtime and ops. revenue can be split or via referral - commercial details later. first step is validating the tech and a pilot.

[05:45] Carlos Mendes: ok pilot. what's a realistic scope?
[05:48] Aisha Patel: 2-3 models, 1-2 customer workloads, 3 weeks of validation: connectivity, benchmark, SLO verification. we provide an eval harness and metrics.

[06:10] Tom Brewer: we have customers using our GPUs with other runtimes; how invasive is integration? we want to avoid heavy kernel maintenance on our side.
[06:18] Aisha Patel: we keep the kernel layer mostly in our runtime but we can collaborate on optimized kernels. maintenance is a joint plan - we push updates and test on partner staging.

[06:40] Sara Li: network - we prefer private peering, not open internet. does redwood require outbound connections?
[06:48] Aisha Patel: for managed control plane we'd need some outbound to telemetry endpoints; for fully private we can operate without outbound, but that triggers air-gap mode and extra install work. we can also do VPC peering and private endpoints.

[07:12] Carlos Mendes: question on data residency - EU customers need data to remain in eu. how do you ensure that for partner-hosted regions?
[07:20] Liam Chen: we support region pinning and routing policies, and we can sign data processing addenda. audit logs and retention controls are configurable per-customer.

[07:45] Priya Kapoor: pricing: is there a partner uplift or margin for partners who resell?
[07:51] Liam Chen: yes, we have partner pricing models. we can discuss ARR/commit vs revenue share. initial pilots usually waived or heavily discounted.

[08:10] Tom Brewer: technical - what telemetry do you collect? is customer PII filtered?
[08:17] Aisha Patel: telemetry is token-level metrics (latency, error rates) and trace IDs. payloads are not stored by default unless customers opt in for logging. PII is filtered and redacted in our hosted offering; for private runs the customer controls logs.

[08:45] Speaker 2: (overlap) - the benchmarks, do you have public numbers?
[08:50] Liam Chen: we publish model profiles but partner numbers vary; we'll share a benchmark sheet and the harness. Aisha will run partner-specific runs.

[09:10] Aisha Patel: quick note on KV cache - it's huge for cost and latency. if your workloads have repeat prefixes we can cache and cut tokens by 30-60% depending. on GPUs this helps throughput.

[09:32] Sara Li: is your runtime open-source or closed?
[09:35] Aisha Patel: closed runtime, but we provide integrations and docs. some tooling libs are OSS.

[10:00] Carlos Mendes: legal - what contracts do you typically need? msas, data processing addenda, maybe a partner agreement.
[10:08] Maya Singh: yes we'll share standard MSA and partner terms; we can do NDA right away if you'd like.

[10:20] Priya Kapoor: for the pilot, who pays infra costs?
[10:24] Liam Chen: usually shared: partner provides hardware and we cover engineering time; in some cases we reimburse a portion or apply credits toward future committed capacity. we'll get commercial specifics after technical validation.

[11:00] Tom Brewer: timeline question - if we wanted to ship a co-branded offering in Q1, is that realistic?
[11:06] Liam Chen: yes plausible if pilot in Nov completes by early Dec and contracting flows in December. Q1 go-to-market is doable.

[11:30] Aisha Patel: can i ask about a few infra details quickly - network MTU, whether you're using SR-IOV, what driver stack for X-1, and cluster scheduler?
[11:40] Sara Li: sure, we run calico, kubernetes 1.26, SR-IOV enabled on select racks. MTU 1500 default but jumbo supported. drivers are upstream with a custom patch set for X-1.

[12:00] Aisha Patel: perfect. we'll include those in the bench plan.

[12:20] [long bit of technical Q&A with specific numbers and small interruptions, some low audio]
[24:40] Aisha Patel: (reading) for the bench we'll need baseline models (gpt-medium, lla-small), sample sequences, concurrency targets and target p95 latency. can you confirm concurrency goals?
[24:52] Tom Brewer: customers target 200 qps for small prompts, and 20 qps for long-form. but we'll scope to a representative workload for the pilot.

[26:00] Carlos Mendes: one risk: support ops - who owns on-call?
[26:06] Liam Chen: joint ownership: for managed runs redwood owns runtime support; partners handle infra hardware failures; we can set escalations.

[29:10] Priya Kapoor: do you do model quantization or do you rely on partner-provided quantized models?
[29:18] Aisha Patel: we recommend quantization profiles but can work with both. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization and batching sets per workload.

[32:05] Carlos Mendes: any red flags from your side?
[32:09] Aisha Patel: nothing major - X-1 will just need the profiler runs. main concerns are network peering and KMS integration timing.

[35:00] Liam Chen: okay quick recap: action items and next steps as we just listed - we'll share deck, benchmark plan, timelines and intro to legal. propose a 3-week pilot with bench targets.

[36:10] Tom Brewer: sounds good. also would like a co-marketing conversation later.

[36:18] Maya Singh: absolutely, we'll sync on GTM if pilot goes well.

[36:25] Speaker 3: (mumbling) can we have an example SLA?

[36:30] Liam Chen: we'll share sample SLAs.

[36:45] Priya Kapoor: any questions from redwood on partner expectations?

[36:48] Carlos Mendes: (laugh) i think that was ours.

[37:00] Aisha Patel: final tech note - we'll want a staging cluster or access to a test rack for kernel tuning. ideally a single node with X-1 and networking prepped.

[37:20] Sara Li: we can carve out a node next week. we'll confirm.

[37:30] Liam Chen: great. i'll send the docs and a proposed pilot statement of work. thanks everyone.

[37:40] Carlos Mendes: thanks, excited.

[37:43] Tom Brewer: thanks all.

[37:47] Meeting end.
